summary: This section explains how pending legal cases and matters are moved from older authorities, like the Company Law Board and various courts, to the new Tribunal. It sets rules for how these transferred cases are handled and when certain appeals can be made. Certain kinds of winding up and reserved cases have special instructions.
points: All matters pending before the Company Law Board on the notified date automatically transfer to the Tribunal.
People unhappy with a Company Law Board decision can appeal to the High Court within sixty days on a question of law.
The High Court can allow up to sixty more days to appeal if the person had a good reason for the delay.
Pending proceedings like arbitration, compromise, and arrangements in District Courts or High Courts move to the Tribunal.
Certain winding up cases move to the Tribunal based on specific stages or if parties apply for transfer under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy rules.
Cases where High Courts have already reserved their final orders stay with the old rules of the 1956 Act.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited had an ongoing legal dispute pending before the Company Law Board. When the Central Government notified the new date, that pending case automatically moved to the Tribunal for final disposal. Meanwhile, Rohit, a shareholder unhappy with an older decision made by the Company Law Board before that date, wanted to challenge it. He filed an appeal before the High Court within the sixty-day time limit on a clear question of law arising from the order. Because Rohit fell ill and missed the initial deadline, the High Court accepted his request and allowed him a further period not exceeding sixty days to file his appeal, as he showed sufficient cause.

terms.meaning: The National Company Law Tribunal, a special body that handles company law cases.
The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
A person who makes a formal appeal to a higher court.
An issue that involves the correct interpretation or application of a law.

watch: Note that not all winding up cases transfer automatically, as some stay under the older 1956 rules depending on their stage or reserved orders.
